description: On the Floor marks the first collaboration between Théophylle Dcx and Maria Silk. In this duet, these two friends attempt to piece together traces of 70s and 80s queer San Francisco. Specifically, their project explores the legacies carried by dance music genres of the late 70s and 80s (especially disco and hi-NRG) in relation to the early days of the HIV/AIDS crisis. The piece weaves together the links between nightlife, the virus, and queer memory, drawing on materials gathered throughout Dcx and Silk’s research: interviews with DJs and clubgoers, Patrick Cowley’s music and personal diaries, live recordings of Sylvester, practices like flagging and fan dancing, and ephemera from clubs like the I-Beam and the Trocadero Transfer. Launched in 2023, WIP was created to give choreographers and performance makers a “low-tech, high-visibility” space to share evolving works with audiences, fostering curiosity, dialogue, and critical exchange at every stage of development. description: tickets SONANCE NO.1 is a 30-minute musical performance featuring a group of collaborating musicians, composed for an audience of humans and plants. Could a musical performance be composed not only to be heard, but to physically participate in the life of another organism? Shall we play the sound of a caterpillar mucnching ? or a Bee buzzing? SONANCE NO.1 invites plants to occupy seats alongside human audience members. Together, they will attend a musical performance in which human reception is no longer the sole measure of the experience, and performers are invited to play for plants whose ways of receiving and responding to sound are uniquely their own. A Road of Many Colors: Two Films on Oscar Rabin & Valentina Kropivnitskaya
description: Oscar Rabin wanted to paint. In the Soviet Union that made him a dissident. In 1974 Rabin helped organize an open-air show of unofficial art in Moscow. The authorities broke it up with bulldozers and water cannons. Images of the attack went around the world, and within weeks officials had to allow a second outdoor show. Thousands came. Several years later Rabin and his wife, the painter Valentina Kropivnitskaya, were forced into exile, and he was stripped of his Soviet citizenship. They started over in France. A Road of Many Colors tells their story in two documentaries written and directed by Alexander Smoljanski and Evgeny Tsymbal.
